title: The inferred energy per element, keeping R and N explicit
spoken: The radiation energy divided by the effective count equals R times B times the frequency divided by N.
explanation: The admitted radiation and independent-point entropy laws fix the effective count and hence this conditional energy scale. The calculation retains the molar constants and does not assume a modern photon-energy formula.
assumptions: Dilute radiation of fixed positive energy in a fixed narrow frequency band obeys the Wien-regime entropy law; deriving that law and its boundary condition remains a separate calculus argument.
The gas comparison assumes independent points with entropy coefficient (R/N)n. Interpreting the shared volume dependence as independent energy elements is a heuristic premise.
R, N, B, frequency and both volumes are positive. The comparison uses unequal volumes so that the common logarithm is nonzero; equal volumes cannot identify the effective count.
The effective count is positive and is not rounded to an integer. The equation establishes a scale within the assumed model, not every property of light.
These are modern teaching equations in SI notation, with B for the paper's beta. The relation h = RB/N is not a premise or conclusion of this check.

notes.title: A conditional energy scale
notes.explanation: Matching the admitted entropy laws determines this scale within the proposed independent-element description.

notes.title: Total energy per effective element
notes.explanation: Divide the positive radiation energy by the effective count inferred from the entropy coefficient.

notes.title: Energy in the band
notes.explanation: The positive total radiation energy in the fixed narrow frequency band.

notes.title: Effective count
notes.explanation: The count that matches the entropy coefficient. It is not rounded and is not a count of individually observed packets.

notes.title: Energy scale with molar constants
notes.explanation: The checked coefficient algebra leaves RBν/N, keeping R and N separate.

notes.title: Gas constant times the spectral scale
notes.explanation: The gas constant multiplies Wien's B and the frequency before division by N.

notes.title: Molar gas constant
notes.explanation: R is the gas constant per mole; division by N supplies the per-element coefficient.

notes.title: Wien's spectral constant
notes.explanation: B is the paper's beta in the admitted Wien-regime entropy law.

notes.title: Fixed frequency
notes.explanation: The narrow band is centered at this positive frequency throughout the volume comparison.

notes.title: Molecular number per mole
notes.explanation: N is positive. It remains explicit instead of being replaced by a modern named constant.
